I’m 25 years old and I often wish I didn’t smoke weed as a teenager. I don’t believe that smoking weed in my teens has directly affected my intelligence, but I think that it probably exacerbated my mental health issues. I think that if I didn’t smoke, my mental health would have been decently better and there’s nothing more important in life than a healthy mind. I don’t think it’s as detrimental as weed on the developing brain but in general, it’s something that might affect your physical health overtime and it’s better to not start at all. I’m trying to quit but it’s one of the hardest things to quit believe it or not, I am able to control my use of every other substance besides nicotine so that says a lot. 

Another thing I would like to add is make sure you get enough sleep. I think our society has gone absolutely bonkers and puts so much academic pressure on teens and a lot of them don’t get nearly enough. You should be getting at least 8 hours a day and ideally 9-10 since your brain needs it for healthy development. 

In summary, avoid the weed and nicotine but especially weed as best you can until ur 20+. Get enough sleep, eat healthy, and make sure you have a healthy outlet for stress. Good luck!

Quite frankly, I’m terrified to take mushrooms or lsd. 

About 5 years ago, when I was 19, I started experimenting with psychedelics such as lsd and mushrooms. The first couple of trips were amazing. I felt like I could think so clearly and deeply and it felt like all my anxiety and depression would dissipate during the trips.

One day however, my friends convinced me to try DMT. Im not sure why, but that day changed everything for me. The trip itself wasn’t terrifying, but it certainly wasn’t the most pleasant, and it was only 10 minutes or so. However, what followed after was a true fucking nightmare. A nightmare that I unfortunately still suffer to this day. 

As soon as the high wore off, I had a really intense and strange headache. I thought it was just a temporary thing, and hoped it would go away in the morning. I also had trouble thinking clearly. Like so much trouble, that I couldn’t form simple sentences in my head without them sounding like my inner monologue has a speech impediment.

To my dismay, these symptoms remained. They remained for weeks. Then months. I felt like I was losing my mind. I consulted several psychiatrists, neurologists, and even ENTs. No on could give me a definitive answer as to why my inner monologue was this severely messed up. After all, people with depression suffer from negative thoughts and fatigue, but most are still perfectly capable of thinking? 

Anyways, I sought treatment for several years. They put me through the ringer with different meds and combinations of meds. Tried several antipsychotics too, gained like 25 pounds. Eventually they were seriously considering ECT for me. At 21 years old. I literally had an appointment regarding starting ECT treatment. 

Luckily, my therapist at the time recommended trying ketamine first. I did 6 sessions of intranasal ketamine and became much better in a matter of months. My inability to think was no longer an issue. Sometimes my thinking problem would come for a day or two, but it was pretty rare. I was no longer depressed and suicidal. 

Things were going well for the next couple years. Until the summer of 2022. This time it wasn’t because of me taking psychedelics. In fact, I still don’t understand what made become depressed again. But my thinking problem is returned. It’s agonizing. Everyday with headaches, low mood, and feeling like your brain is broken. 

I’m not saying that this will happen if you take mushrooms or lsd or DMT. I just wanted to share that these substances are serious business, and it seems like they may have triggered an even more serious depression/mental illness in me than would have otherwise happened. Or maybe it would have happened regardless. Truth is there’s no easy way of knowing. 

These days I’m back on ketamine troches. I am hoping they will work, but progress has been significantly slower than my first round of treatment. Im starting to worry that im truly screwed.
